chunks: he (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so after that, Yaqoub (peace be upon him) used to get his caller to call out during every morning, from his house, upon a Farsakh (about four miles), “Indeed! The one who wants the lunch, so let him come to Yaqoub (peace be upon him)!” And when it was evening, he called out, “Indeed! The one who wants the dinner, so let him come to Yaqoub (peace be upon him)!”'.

key_terms.فَرْسَخٍ: Farsakh (a unit of distance, approx. 4 miles)

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Yaqoub demonstrate hospitality to his neighbors?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical application of neighborly rights through Prophet Yaqoub’s (peace be upon him) daily public invitation for meals, a practice that underscores the Islamic emphasis on communal bonding and generosity. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often cited to illustrate that hospitality is not merely a private virtue but a public duty that strengthens social ties and ensures no neighbor is left in need.
